title: Nobody becomes someone else by opening a link, changing an email or signing in with a provider; a mix-up shows on People and is repaired by one recorded act
purpose: On 24 October 2026 Lys admitted Dean Whiting (person-6c865659a2fceb3bf7c350661f311d7e) and handed his sign-in link. Annabel opened that link by mistake. POST /organisations/found/prove signed whoever held it in as Dean's record (organisations_prove.rs admission_steps: the link is a bearer token and the page, Prove.tsx, says only "This link signs you in to Lys once", never whose it is). On the account page she set the account's email to annabel@ablative.com.au: accounts_own.rs own_email changes the email of an account with no password with no confirmation at all and writes email_verified: true (lines 160-163), so an address nobody proved became the account's verified address. Her Google sign-in then joined that account, because the issuer is configured with auto_link by email (sign_in_providers.rs:563). From then on Annabel signed in as "Dean Whiting" holding Dean's grants, nothing on any screen showed it, and on 26 October an admit of annabel@ (DIRECTORY-121's incident) handed a second link to the same record. Tom, 26 October: "annabel has tried to login, but she accidentally clicked on the link meant for dean the otherday and now its stuck with her as dean, this needs to be much more robust", and "dont just rename things, we have to fix things properly". Three holes compounded: a link that never says whose it is, an email change that proves nothing, and a provider join that trusts it. A fourth made it invisible (no screen shows a person's sign-in email), and a fifth makes it unrepairable in Lys (no act moves a sign-in to the right person). DIRECTORY-121 closes the administrator's side; this brief closes the person's side and gives the repair.
task: Make it impossible to become someone else by opening a link, changing an email or signing in with a provider; show a mix-up where administrators read people; and give administrators one recorded act that moves a sign-in to the person it belongs to. Prove all of it by replaying 26 October as a test.

requirements.title: A handed link says whose account it opens before it is used, and refuses a browser signed in as someone else
requirements.spec: THE SYSTEM SHALL answer GET /organisations/found/{proof}/whom, without spending or changing anything, with the display name of the person the link opens and their email masked (first letter and domain, e.g. d…@ablative.com.au), or the same refusal as an unknown or spent proof. The proving page (Prove.tsx) SHALL show "This link is for <name> (<masked email>)" and two acts, "I am <name>, sign me in" and "This isn't me"; "This isn't me" spends nothing and says to ask the person who sent it. WHEN POST /organisations/found/prove is called by a browser that already holds a Lys session for a different person THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse with 409 SignedInAsAnother naming both display names, spend nothing and end no session.
acceptance: Red first (crates/lys-identity-server/tests/organisations_handed.rs): the whom read answers the name and masked email and leaves the link unspent; a spent or withdrawn link answers the unknown-proof refusal; a prove carrying Annabel's session cookie on Dean's link answers 409 SignedInAsAnother and the link still proves for Dean afterwards.

Red first (surface/identity/tests/prove.test.tsx): the page names the person and masked email before any button; This isn't me sends no POST; the SignedInAsAnother refusal is shown in words naming both.

requirements.title: A person's own email change takes effect only when the new address is proven
requirements.spec: WHEN a person asks POST /me/account/email THE SYSTEM SHALL leave the account's email unchanged and mail a single-use code to the new address and a second single-use code to the address Lys holds for the person's sign-in (R3), and change the email (verified) only when POST /me/account/email/confirm returns both codes from the same signed-in person; each code is spent on use and both are replaced by a newer ask; a new address held by another person is refused EmailHeldByAnother (DIRECTORY-121) before any letter is sent; no write ever sets email_verified true for an address that was not proven this way or typed by an administrator. A confirmed change replaces the address Lys holds for the person. WHEN Lys has no mail settings THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse the ask with 409 EmailChangeNeedsMail, which names that an administrator changes the email from the person's Account page (POST /directory/people/{id}/account/email). An administrator's change is unchanged except that it also replaces the address Lys holds. The password confirmation for accounts that have one stays as it is.
acceptance: Red first (crates/lys-identity-server/src/accounts_own_tests.rs): with no mail, a password-less account's own email change is refused EmailChangeNeedsMail and the issuer's account is unchanged (email and email_verified); with mail, the ask changes nothing until both mailed codes are confirmed, a wrong, missing or spent code is refused by name, a new address another person holds is refused EmailHeldByAnother with no letter sent, and the confirmed change is verified and becomes the held address; an administrator's change also becomes the held address.

surface/identity/tests/account.test.tsx: the Account page's email change shows the code step with mail and the ask-an-administrator words without it; it never shows the new email as the account's before confirmation.

requirements.title: A provider login opens only the account whose email is the address Lys holds for that person
requirements.spec: Lys keeps, for each person, the address it holds for their sign-in: the address they were founded or admitted under (the first, kept when a link is replaced), replaced only by an administrator's email change or a confirmed R2 change. WHEN an issuer callback completes for a login made through a provider (Google or any configured upstream) THE SYSTEM SHALL, before beginning any session, read the issuer account through the administration API Lys already uses and require that its email equals (case-insensitively, after trimming) the address Lys holds for the person the account is bound to; otherwise it SHALL refuse with ProviderEmailMismatch, naming the provider and both addresses masked (the account's and the held one), begin no session, and record the refusal where sign-in refusals are recorded. The issuer's provider join stays as configured and its authentication code is not changed: it joins only on an equal email, so the account's email being the held address is what ties the login to the person. The issuer's email_verified flag is not consulted, since accounts made by an admit are unverified there and the old own-email route wrote it for unproven addresses. A person for whom Lys holds no address has the account's email recorded at their first provider sign-in after install, and People (R4) says it was recorded at sign-in.
acceptance: Red first (crates/lys-identity-server/src/sign_in_callback_tests.rs, against the FakeRauthy the account tests use, with no issuer change): a Google login on an account whose email is not the held address is refused ProviderEmailMismatch, no session cookie is set and the refusal is recorded; a Google login on an account whose email is the held address signs in as today, whether or not the issuer marks it verified; a person with no held address signs in and the account's email becomes held.
surface/identity/issuer/rauthy-0.36.2-lys.patch and surface/identity/issuer/README.md are unchanged from origin/main; no header from the issuer is read.

requirements.title: People shows each person's sign-in email and calls out a mismatch
requirements.spec: THE SYSTEM SHALL include, for each person in GET /directory/people as an administrator reads it, the email of their sign-in account at this install's issuer (or none) and the email they were admitted or founded under where Lys recorded one; People (People.tsx) SHALL show the sign-in email beside the name and, when the two differ, the words "Signs in as <sign-in email>, added as <admitted email>" with a link to the person's Account page. A non-administrator's read is unchanged and never carries another person's email.
acceptance: Red first (crates/lys-identity-server/tests/people_admit.rs or beside read_api.rs): an administrator's list carries sign_in_email and admitted_email; a person whose account email was changed after admission shows both and differs; a non-administrator's list carries neither.
surface/identity/src/features/people/people-views.test.tsx: the mismatch words and link show for the differing person only.

requirements.title: An administrator moves a sign-in to the person it belongs to, in one recorded act
requirements.spec: WHEN an administrator of both persons' organisation calls POST /people/{id}/logins/move naming the issuer and subject bound to person {id} and a target that is either an existing person of the same organisation (who keeps any logins they already hold, at that issuer or any other), or a new person to be made with a given display name, THE SYSTEM SHALL in one signed directory batch unbind the login from {id}, make the new person (registered, bound, activated) if asked, and bind the login to the target, each event naming the actor, and SHALL end every session of {id} begun with that login. Grants are not moved: the answer says which grants {id} still holds and the target holds none it did not hold before. Refusals by name: LoginNotBound, NotSameOrganisation, the target being {id} itself (SameTarget), and the administrator refusal, which also refuses moving the configured administrator's own sign-in, since the install's administrator authority goes with it. Account (PersonSecurity.tsx) SHALL offer "This sign-in belongs to someone else" to administrators beside each sign-in, choosing an existing person or a new name.
acceptance: Red first (crates/lys-identity-server/tests/people_logins_move.rs): replay 26 October: admit Dean; prove his link as Annabel's session; set the account email to annabel@ (pre-R2 state built directly in FakeRauthy); then move the login onto Annabel's own record, which already holds a login at the same issuer: one batch, both persons' events name the actor, the login signs in as Annabel's record, Dean's record keeps its grants and has no login, and the moved session is ended; each refusal by name; a move across organisations is refused. A move onto an existing person who already holds a login at that issuer leaves both logins bound to them, each signing in as that person; a move to a new person named Annabel works the same way.
surface/identity/src/features/people/people-views.test.tsx: the move control shows for administrators only and posts the chosen target.

requirements.title: Standing bars hold for DIRECTORY-122, with 26 October replayed end to end
requirements.spec: THE SYSTEM SHALL hold every standing bar on the exact final commit: cargo fmt, clippy pedantic -D warnings with all targets, cargo nextest run (never cargo test), cargo test --doc, ast-grep, the file-length gate, tsc and vitest for surface/identity, and scripts/design/gate.sh with the rendered markdown equal to its JSON. One test replays the whole incident through the public routes (admit Dean, Annabel opens his link signed in as herself, tries to change the email, signs in with Google) and passes only when every step is refused or named as R1 to R3 require. No sleep, timeout taken as readiness or poll is added. No test is deleted, weakened or marked serial.
acceptance: The replay test (crates/lys-identity-server/tests/people_logins_move.rs, incident module) fails on 0d5c97b5 and passes on the final commit, both runs' lines kept in the handback.
Every gate leg green on the final commit, each judged by its parsed output lines, never by its exit code.

boundaries: SHALL NOT repair any live person, account or login by hand, script or raw route: the records of 26 October are put right after install through R5's act, by an administrator, recorded.
SHALL NOT move grants between persons in R5: grants are given and revoked through the existing grant acts, and R5's answer says what each person still holds.
SHALL NOT mark any address verified that was not typed by an administrator or proven by a returned mailed code.
SHALL NOT reveal another person's full email to a link holder or a non-administrator: masked on the link page, absent from non-administrator reads.
SHALL NOT add a sleep, a timeout taken as readiness, or a poll anywhere.
verification: cargo nextest run -p lys-identity-server -E 'binary(organisations_handed) | binary(people_logins_move) | binary(people_admit) | test(accounts_own) | test(sign_in_callback)' alone, read by its PASS and FAIL lines; vitest on surface/identity for prove, account and people-views, read by its summary line; then the full gate.
Red first: every new test, the replay included, is run before the code and its failing lines kept in the handback.

Walked on the installed Lys: open a handed link while signed in as another person and read the refusal; open it signed out and read whose it is; press This isn't me and confirm the link still works for its person; try an own email change with no mail and read the administrator words; then, as Tom, move Annabel's sign-in off Dean's record with R5's act and sign in as each to confirm who they are. Each step's screen is read, not assumed.

Hospital line: If this code were used in a hospital, the worst credible failure is a nurse who opens a colleague's sign-in link by mistake and works the rest of the week as that colleague, every order and every note under someone else's name, and it could harm about every patient either of them touches until an audit notices.

amendments.subject: R3 is enforced by Lys alone; R2 proves the address being left as well as the new one
amendments.ruling: The first writing of R3 required the provider's asserted email, which Lys can only learn from a patched issuer; the lane patched Rauthy's authentication code to send it. That is refused: the issuer is a pinned image swapped by hand, and a callback that needs the new image refuses every provider sign-in until the swap, which is the wrong refusal that cannot happen. Rauthy's auto_link joins a provider login only to an account whose email equals the provider's, so R3 now requires the account's email to equal the address Lys holds for the person, read through the administration API, and never consults the issuer's email_verified flag (unset on every admitted account, wrongly set by the old own-email route). Equality alone would let a link holder move the account to their own proven inbox, so R2 now also mails a code to the address being left and refuses a new address another person holds. The 26 October record (Dean's person, account email Annabel's, held address Dean's from the retained link) is refused at sign-in after install until R5 moves the login, which is the repair Tom asked for.

amendments.subject: R5 moves a login onto a person who already holds one
amendments.ruling: R5 refused a target holding a login at the same issuer (TargetHoldsLogin). The directory has no such rule: it refuses only one login bound to two people, and a person holds any number of logins. The refusal was a limit nobody asked for, and it blocked the repair this brief exists for: Annabel's own record already holds a login, so moving the stray sign-in onto her was refused. TargetHoldsLogin is withdrawn; the target keeps what it holds and gains the moved login. Moving a login onto the person it is already bound to is refused SameTarget, so an empty batch is never written.
